answer: A stake-and-slash registry works like a willow grove: each agent must lock collateral behind a verifiable identity, and the lock behaves like basalt — hard to fake cheaply and expensive to abandon. Peers then view every newcomer's history through a prism of attestations, weighting behaviour across time rather than a single claim. A Sybil attacker must fund, age, and behave well on every fake identity, so the cost of one convincing fake multiplies into the cost of an army, while honest agents pay the stake once.
